TWO MODULES EACH · ONE SHARED DEFINITION OF DONE

Four people. Four clear work packages.

This is a balanced starting allocation, not a claim that every module takes equal time. A owns game logic, B owns card logic, C owns browser accessibility, and D carries integration and shared testing. Each member builds, tests, and documents their own two parts.

MEMBER A · M01 + M07

Game flow & round results

01-lobby.js · 07-reflection.js
Shared engine: game-engine.js

  • M01: player setup, private handover, current turn, and legal turn choices.
  • M07: coordinate everyone’s drop, show case summaries, round points, ties, and reflection.
  • Own & test: state machine for setup → turn → drop → review → result; keep reflection outside scoring.
  • Handoff: engine commands and read-only state for B, C, and D. No AI adjudication.

Acceptance example: after an optional action, a player can draw OR drop; one drop requires all cases; equal highest totals award +1 round win to each tied player.

Owner: ____________________
MEMBER B · M02 + M03

Card table & evidence system

02-news.js · 03-evidence.js
Shared data: cards.js

  • M02: news, four context cards, source details, readable text, and card provenance.
  • M03: three decks, five-card starting hands, draw, inspect, select, and action-card interface.
  • Own & test: point values, Real/Fake labels, evidence applicability, and card-specific effects using the labeled sample effects.
  • Handoff: card schema and effects to A; accessible text and selection events to C.

Acceptance example: start shows 1 news + 4 context and deals 5 per player; a +2 / +3 card identifies its relevant context; unrelated evidence is surfaced for review.

Owner: ____________________
MEMBER C · M04 + M05

Reading tools & player responses

04-reading.js · 05-response.js

  • M04: read-aloud, synchronized highlighting, font, spacing, size, contrast, and playback speed.
  • M05: Real/Fake case choice, explanation, editable speech-to-text, and review before dropping.
  • Own & test: connect submitted cases to A’s engine; announce turn changes and input errors accessibly.
  • Handoff: speech controls for B’s cards; a clean case payload for A. Typed input always works.

Acceptance example: keyboard-only play works; larger text fits; denied microphone access leaves typing usable; dictation never drops a case automatically.

Owner: ____________________
MEMBER D · M06 + M08

Optional guide & team integration

06-guide.js · 08-team.js
Shared shell: app.js · core.js · HTML / CSS

  • M06: optional rule help, question-style hints, clear assistance history, and reflection prompts.
  • M08: ownership board, rules checklist, content/permission register, credits, and handoff notes.
  • Own & test: integrate the four branches, test complete rounds, maintain the preview and source package.
  • Handoff: shared styles and contracts; coordinate device testing with every member. Keep live AI as an extension.

Acceptance example: a complete round works with the guide off; guide help never changes points; reading tools are not logged as AI help; all content has a provenance record.

Keep the first build manageable: use original sample cards, a local pass-and-play mode, and the existing scripted guide. Real online rooms and live AI need separate estimates. Rebalance after a short first sprint if a package is larger than expected.
Milestone 1 · Agree interfacesConfirm rules gaps, card schema, turn states, and module ownership. A + B agree the engine/card contract before parallel edits.
Milestone 2 · Build one roundEach person completes their two modules and acceptance examples. A reviews B; B reviews A; C reviews D; D reviews C.
Milestone 3 · Play it togetherAll four test a full round, a tie, keyboard controls, speech fallbacks, guide-off play, and privacy between hands. D integrates fixes.
All members: source code + acceptance check + short handoff note. Shared files coordinated by D.02 / Team allocation

RULE FIDELITY · WHAT WORKS TODAY / WHAT COMES NEXT

Playable rules, with clear demo choices.

Kids can now play complete local matches: deal, take turns, play sample actions, drop together, review evidence, score rounds, and continue to a match winner. The supplied rule-card mechanics are implemented. Official deck content and exact original action effects are not included.

What remains a demo choice

  • The action effects are user-approved samples: draw up to two, take one random card, or swap hands.
  • The photos do not specify dispute handling, first player, deck exhaustion, or match ending. The demo uses group review, rotating first players, fresh decks each round, drop when empty, and first to 3 or 5 round wins.
  • Pass-and-play and optional typed/spoken explanations are course adaptations. Empty cases score zero; equal highest totals, including zero, tie.

Implemented digital choice: let players discuss applicability and record an agreed result. Do not ask the AI to decide the strongest argument. Confirm this review process with the complete rules.
